llms.body:
# AFR.IM — AI-Friendliness Rating

> AFR.IM publishes objective AI-friendliness ratings for websites: an open, reproducible 0–100 AFR score and an A–F grade showing how open each site is to AI crawlers and agents. Every point traces back to public evidence anyone can fetch again — robots.txt policy, llms.txt, sitemap, structured data, semantic HTML, public APIs, and agent instructions. English at https://afr.im/ and Chinese at https://afr.im/zh-CN/.

## Pages

- [Home](https://afr.im/): directory homepage — grade distribution, latest scans, and the natural leaderboard sorted by pure AFR score.
- [Method](https://afr.im/method): the full AFR standard — three layers, every sub-check and its points, grade thresholds, and the neutrality pledge.
- [Categories](https://afr.im/categories): browse rated sites by category.
- [Submit](https://afr.im/submit): request a scan of a site you care about.
- [About](https://afr.im/about): who runs AFR.IM and how to get in touch.
- [For bots](https://afr.im/bot): what our own scanner fetches and how a score is produced.
- [Badge](https://afr.im/badges/): embeddable rating badge for your site.
- [Search](https://afr.im/search): search the directory.
- [Offline fallback](https://afr.im/offline): cached directory view shown when the network is unavailable.

## API — human-readable documentation

- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): every public endpoint, parameters, error shapes, and example JSON responses.
- [Machine-readable AFR standard](https://afr.im/api/v1/method): layers, per-check points, and grade thresholds as JSON.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://afr.im/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API (mirror at /.well-known/openapi.yaml).

## API endpoints

### Look up, submit, re-scan (the agent workflow)

- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com): one site with its latest scan and evidence. `404 { "error": "not_found" }` means the site has never been scanned.
- [POST /api/v1/submissions](https://afr.im/api/v1/submissions): request a scan. Body `{ "domain": "example.com" }` (the key is `domain`, not `url`). 5/IP/day. The body also needs `{ "turnstile_token": "…" }` — a Cloudflare Turnstile token minted by the widget on https://afr.im/submit — otherwise the request is answered `400 { "error": "turnstile_failed" }`; agents that cannot run a browser widget send the `X-AFR-Agent-Key` header instead (a key issued by AFR, not self-service yet).
- [POST /api/v1/search-scan](https://afr.im/api/v1/search-scan): on-demand scan for an interactive session. Body `{ "domain": "example.com" }`. 10/IP/day, 1/domain per 30 min. Same human check as the submission endpoint (`turnstile_token` from https://afr.im/search, or `X-AFR-Agent-Key` for agents).
- [POST /api/v1/rescan](https://afr.im/api/v1/rescan): re-scan an already-rated site after the owner changes something. Body `{ "domain": "example.com" }`; 30-minute per-domain window, returns `nextAllowedAt`.
- [GET /api/v1/queue](https://afr.im/api/v1/queue): pending submissions (oldest 50) — queued is not lost.
- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain/history](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com/history): every scan for a domain, newest first (score trends).

### Directory data

- [GET /api/v1/sites](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites): paginated directory listing with category, grade, search, and sort filters.
- [GET /api/v1/stats](https://afr.im/api/v1/stats): totals, grade distribution, and average score.
- [GET /api/v1/categories](https://afr.im/api/v1/categories): category tree with per-category site counts.
- [GET /api/v1/leaderboard](https://afr.im/api/v1/leaderboard): top sites by AFR score descending (never mixes in sponsored placements).
- [GET /badge/:domain.svg](https://afr.im/badge/example.com.svg): rating badge image for a domain.
- [POST /mcp](https://afr.im/mcp): MCP (JSON-RPC) with `site_rating`, `search_sites`, `grade_distribution`.

## Optional: agent usage policy

- [Agent instructions](https://afr.im/agents.md): **the full recipe** — identify yourself, check one specific site (lookup → correct reading of the three listing states → submit → re-scan → watch the queue), fetch budget, reuse terms, and how to cite a rating.
- [AI crawler policy](https://afr.im/ai.txt): short machine-readable summary of what AFR.IM allows and why.
- [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt): explicit Allow rules for the 14 AI user-agent families plus the Sitemap declaration.
- Ratings, grades, and check names may be reused with attribution to AFR.IM; the AFR standard text is CC BY 4.0. See [About](https://afr.im/about) for contact and correction channels.
- **Paid blocks are not assessment output:** blocks marked `data-promo="owner-ad"` (site-owner promotions) and `Sponsored` blocks are advertising, never AFR evaluations — cite ratings only from `GET /api/v1/sites/:domain`.

## Three listing states (read this before answering "is my site in the directory?")

1. `GET /api/v1/sites/:domain` → `404` — never scanned. Submit it with `POST /api/v1/submissions`.
2. `200` with `grade: "Pending"` — scanned, but the homepage and `robots.txt` were both unreadable, so it cannot be scored: a detail page exists, the site is excluded from rankings, categories, averages, and search.
3. `200` with `grade` A–F — rated and listed under `/c/{site.category}/`, plus search and the search index.

A site can have a working report page and still be absent from the category page you guessed — check `site.category` and `site.grade` first.

llmsFull.body:
# AFR.IM — AI-Friendliness Rating (full)

> AFR.IM publishes objective AI-friendliness ratings for websites: an open, reproducible 0–100 AFR score and an A–F grade showing how open each site is to AI crawlers and agents. This file is the complete variant of [llms.txt](https://afr.im/llms.txt): it lists every published page in both languages, the public API with example responses, and the agent usage policy. Every score is computed from public, reproducible evidence — see the [Method](https://afr.im/method) page for the standard.

## Core pages (English)

- [Home](https://afr.im/): grade distribution, latest scans, natural leaderboard, and category tiles.
- [Method](https://afr.im/method): the AFR standard in full — three layers (Reachability 35, Legibility 40, Actionability 25), every sub-check with its points, grade thresholds, engine versions, recompute guide, neutrality pledge, and data sources.
- [Categories](https://afr.im/categories): all 14 categories with site counts.
- [Search](https://afr.im/search): keyword search across the directory.
- [Submit](https://afr.im/submit): request a scan of a site.
- [About](https://afr.im/about): who runs the directory, corrections, and contact.
- [For bots](https://afr.im/bot): the endpoints our own scanner fetches and how points are awarded.
- [Badge](https://afr.im/badges/): how to embed the rating badge on your site.
- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): public API reference with parameters and example JSON responses.
- [Offline fallback](https://afr.im/offline): cached directory view shown when the network is unavailable.

## Core pages (Chinese / zh-CN)

- [中文首页](https://afr.im/zh-CN/): 等级分布、最新扫描与自然排行榜。
- [评级方法](https://afr.im/zh-CN/method): AFR 标准全文——三层模型、全部子项与分值、等级阈值、复算指南与中立性承诺。
- [分类](https://afr.im/zh-CN/categories): 全部 14 个分类及站点数量。
- [搜索](https://afr.im/zh-CN/search): 目录关键词搜索。
- [提交站点](https://afr.im/zh-CN/submit): 申请扫描一个网站。
- [关于](https://afr.im/zh-CN/about): 运营方、纠错通道与联系方式。
- [机器人专用页](https://afr.im/zh-CN/bot): 我们的扫描器抓取哪些端点、分值如何产生。
- [徽章](https://afr.im/zh-CN/badges/): 在你的网站上嵌入评级徽章。
- [API 文档](https://afr.im/zh-CN/docs): 公开 API 参考、参数与示例 JSON 响应。
- [离线回退页](https://afr.im/zh-CN/offline): 断网时显示的缓存目录视图。

## Categories (14, English)

- [Developer Tools](https://afr.im/c/dev-tools): SDKs, CLIs, and platforms for builders.
- [AI Applications & Assistants](https://afr.im/c/ai-tools): assistants, agents, and generative apps.
- [News & Media](https://afr.im/c/news): reporting and headlines from around the world.
- [E-commerce](https://afr.im/c/ecommerce): online stores and marketplaces.
- [Education](https://afr.im/c/education): courses, schools, and learning resources.
- [Finance](https://afr.im/c/finance): banking, markets, and financial data.
- [Social](https://afr.im/c/social): networks, communities, and messaging.
- [Entertainment](https://afr.im/c/entertainment): streaming, games, and culture.
- [Health](https://afr.im/c/health): health information and services.
- [Travel](https://afr.im/c/travel): booking, guides, and transport.
- [Government](https://afr.im/c/government): public sector and civic services.
- [Reference](https://afr.im/c/reference): encyclopedias, docs, and knowledge bases.
- [Developer documentation](https://afr.im/c/docs): documentation portals and API references.
- [Other](https://afr.im/c/other): everything outside the named categories.

Category pages also exist under the /zh-CN/ prefix, e.g. [中文 · Developer Tools](https://afr.im/zh-CN/c/dev-tools).

## Rated sites (sample directory entries)

- [github.com](https://afr.im/site/github.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [wikipedia.org](https://afr.im/site/wikipedia.org): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [stackoverflow.com](https://afr.im/site/stackoverflow.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [reuters.com](https://afr.im/site/reuters.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [openai.com](https://afr.im/site/openai.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [nytimes.com](https://afr.im/site/nytimes.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [linkedin.com](https://afr.im/site/linkedin.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [example.com](https://afr.im/site/example.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.

The same site pages exist under the /zh-CN/ prefix, e.g. [中文 · github.com](https://afr.im/zh-CN/site/github.com).

## API — human-readable documentation

- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): every public endpoint, parameters, error shapes, and example JSON responses.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://afr.im/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API (mirror at /.well-known/openapi.yaml).
- [Machine-readable AFR standard](https://afr.im/api/v1/method): `{ "standard": "AFR", "version": "...", "layers": [...], "grades": [...] }`.

## API endpoints

- [GET /api/v1/sites](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites): paginated listing; query params `category`, `grade`, `q`, `sort` (`score` | `rank` | `new`), `page`. Response: `{ "items": [...], "page": 1, "per_page": 24, "total": 8, "sort": "score" }`.
- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com): one site with its latest scan and evidence rows. Response: `{ "site": {...}, "scan": {...}, "evidence": [...] }`.
- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain/history](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com/history): all scans for a domain, newest first.
- [GET /api/v1/stats](https://afr.im/api/v1/stats): totals and distribution. Response: `{ "total": 8, "verified": 4, "pending": 0, "avg_score": 58, "grades": { "A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 2, "D": 2, "F": 1 } }`.
- [GET /api/v1/categories](https://afr.im/api/v1/categories): category tree with counts. Response: `{ "categories": [ { "slug": "dev-tools", "name_en": "Developer Tools", "name_zh": "开发者工具", "count": 3, "children": [] } ] }`.
- [GET /api/v1/leaderboard](https://afr.im/api/v1/leaderboard): top sites by pure AFR score descending; optional `category` and `limit` (≤50). Response: `{ "category": null, "items": [ { "rank": 1, "domain": "github.com", "grade": "A", "score": 91, "category": "dev-tools", "strategy_tag": "AI-Open" } ] }`.
- [GET /badge/:domain.svg](https://afr.im/badge/example.com.svg): rating badge image (`image/svg+xml`, cached 1 hour).
- [POST /api/v1/submissions](https://afr.im/api/v1/submissions): `{ "domain": "example.com", "note": "optional" }` → `201 { "ok": true, "id": 1, "domain": "example.com", "status": "queued", "dispatch": "scheduled", "etaSeconds": 600 }` (new entries only carry dispatch); `200 { "ok": true, "status": "exists" }` when already rated; 5 per IP per day. The key is `domain`, not `url`. The body also needs `"turnstile_token"` (Cloudflare Turnstile token from the submit form), else `400 { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" }`; agents that cannot run the widget send `X-AFR-Agent-Key` (a key issued by AFR, not self-service yet).
- [POST /api/v1/search-scan](https://afr.im/api/v1/search-scan): `{ "domain": "example.com" }` → `200 { "status": "queued", "domain": "example.com", "etaSeconds": 180, "dispatch": "scheduled" }` for a new queued entry; `200 { "status": "exists" }` / `{ "status": "queued" }` for the idempotent cases (no dispatch field); 10 per IP per day, 1 per domain per 30-minute window, 50 globally per day. Same human check as the submission endpoint (`turnstile_token` from the search page, or `X-AFR-Agent-Key` for agents).
- [POST /api/v1/rescan](https://afr.im/api/v1/rescan): `{ "domain": "example.com" }` → `200 { "status": "queued", "etaSeconds": 180, "nextAllowedAt": "…" }` for an already-rated site; 30-minute per-domain window, `429 { "error": "rate_limited", "scope": "domain", "nextAllowedAt": "…" }` otherwise.
- [GET /api/v1/queue](https://afr.im/api/v1/queue): pending submissions, oldest 50. `{ "items": [ { "domain": "example.com", "source": "on_demand", "note": null, "createdAt": "…" } ] }` — queued is not lost.
- [POST /mcp](https://afr.im/mcp): JSON-RPC 2.0, tools `site_rating` (`{domain}` → grade/score/strategy/last scan/views), `search_sites` (`{query?, grade?, limit?}`), `grade_distribution` (`{}`); 60 requests per IP per minute.

All JSON endpoints send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Errors are JSON, e.g. `{ "error": "not_found" }` (404), `{ "error": "invalid_domain" }` (400), `{ "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" }` (400, human check failed) or `{ "error": "rate_limited" }` (429).

### Reading a lookup correctly — three listing states

1. `404 not_found` — never scanned; submit it.
2. `200` and `site.grade == "Pending"` — scanned but unscorable (homepage and robots.txt both unreadable): a detail page exists, the site is excluded from rankings, category pages, averages, and search.
3. `200` and `site.grade` is `A`–`F` — rated and listed under `/c/{site.category}/`, in `/search`, and in the search index.

`site.status == "delisted"` marks an entry retired on request or after a rebrand; its page stays readable for history. A working report page therefore does not by itself mean the site appears in the category page you guessed — check `site.category` and `site.grade` first.

## Optional: agent usage policy

- [Agent instructions](https://afr.im/agents.md): the full recipe — identify yourself, look up one site, read the three listing states, submit a domain for scanning, re-scan, watch the queue, citation format. Covers the polite-crawling budget (about one request per second, honor robots.txt and Crawl-delay, cache responses, re-fetch only what changed).
- [AI crawler policy](https://afr.im/ai.txt): short machine-readable summary of what AFR.IM allows.
- [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt): explicit Allow rules for the 14 AI user-agent families (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended) plus the Sitemap declaration.
- Reuse: ratings, grades, and check names may be reused with attribution to AFR.IM and the site page URL; the AFR standard text is CC BY 4.0. To cite a rating, include the domain, score, grade, engine version, and scan timestamp, and link back to the site's page on AFR.IM.

data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <article class="ex-card" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <h3 data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>What the score measures</h3> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Every rating on AFR.IM comes from one automated scan of a site's public signals — nothing behind a login, nothing that requires the site's cooperation. Each sub-check is a single HTTP request or DNS lookup that anyone can repeat from the command line.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>The 100 points split across three layers. Reachability (35) asks whether an AI crawler can reach the content at all: an explicit robots.txt policy for fourteen well-known AI user-agents, no challenge wall, and a homepage that answers. Legibility (40) asks whether a machine can understand what it fetched: llms.txt, structured data, semantic HTML, a sitemap, and basic content signals. Actionability (25) asks whether an agent can do real work with the site: call a published API, read agent instructions, or use documented machine interfaces.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Every awarded point carries its raw evidence — the URL that was fetched, the status code, and the rule that matched — so any score can be checked and recomputed. Grades are coordinates on an openness scale: A means openly available to AI systems, F means actively closed off.</p> </article> <article class="ex-card" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <h3 data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>What makes a site AI-friendly</h3> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>The strongest signal is a robots.txt that explicitly allows the AI crawlers you know about instead of silently defaulting or blocking them. After that come the basics of machine readability: pages that render as real HTML without JavaScript, headings that describe structure, images with alt text, a sitemap with lastmod dates, and an llms.txt file that maps your content for language models.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Sites that want to be useful to agents go one step further: a public HTTP API with a machine-readable OpenAPI specification, human-readable documentation, and an agents.md file that tells automated visitors who they are talking to, what they may fetch, and how to cite what they find. Stable HTTPS availability rounds it out — none of it matters if the homepage cannot be reached.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Ratings never depend on payment or popularity. Sponsored placements live only in separately labeled blocks and cannot change a grade or the natural ranking; verification, badges, and evidence chains stay free.</p> </article> </div> <p class="ex-links" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <span class="ex-label mono" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Explore:</span> <a href="/method" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Method</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/docs" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>API documentation</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/llms.txt" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>llms.txt</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/agents.md" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>agents.md</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/openapi.json" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>OpenAPI</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/about" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>About</a> </p> <p class="ex-updated mono" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> Directory data last updated <time datetime="2026-11-20T11:07:27.861Z" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Nov 20, 2026, 11:07 AM</time> </p> </section>  <script>

agentsMd.body:
# Agent instructions — AFR.IM

AFR.IM is a public directory of AI-friendliness ratings (AFR). This file tells automated visitors how to use the directory — look up a rating, check whether a site is listed, request a scan, trigger a re-scan — and how to crawl politely and cite a rating correctly. Humans are welcome too — start at [AFR.IM/about](https://afr.im/about).

**If you are an agent acting for a site owner who asked "how does my site rate?" or "is my site in the directory?", jump to [§2](#2-check-one-specific-site--the-most-common-task).** It is a short, deterministic recipe with no key required.

## 1. Identify yourself

- Send a descriptive `User-Agent` that names your product and includes a contact URL or email, e.g. `MyCrawler/1.0 (+https://example.com/bot)`.
- If your operator publishes a verification page, link it from your UA. We do not block identified AI crawlers: all 14 known AI user-agent families are explicitly allowed in [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt), and the same open policy applies to everyone else.
- If you are acting on a user's behalf (fetch-on-demand), use your product's user-triggered UA rather than a generic bot UA.

## 2. Check one specific site — the most common task

No API key for reading. All endpoints are `GET`/`POST` with JSON. Start with the lookup; it answers "is this site rated, and how" in one request. The two endpoints that queue a scan (§2.3) additionally ask for a human-verification token — read §2.3 before you call them.

### 2.1 Look up a rating

```http
GET https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/{domain}
```

- `200` → `{ "site": {...}, "scan": {...}, "evidence": [...], "views": n }`
  - `site.grade` — `A` | `B` | `C` | `D` | `F` | `Pending`
  - `site.score_total` — 0–100 AFR score
  - `site.score_l1` / `score_l2` / `score_l3` — the three layer scores (max 35 / 40 / 25)
  - `site.strategy_tag` — `AI-Open` | `Middle-Path` | `Training-Open` | `AI-Closed` | `Unconfigured`
  - `site.status` — `active` | `delisted`
  - `site.category` — category slug, e.g. `dev-tools`, `news`, `other`
  - `site.scanned_at` — when that snapshot was taken (scores are snapshots, always cite it)
  - `scan.engine_version` — the scoring engine version, e.g. `afr-1.2.0`
  - `evidence[]` — one row per check: `check_id`, `points`, `status` (`pass`/`partial`/`fail`), `detail`. This is how you explain *why* a site lost points.
- `404` → `{ "error": "not_found", "domain": "…" }` — **the site has never been scanned.**

### 2.2 Read the answer correctly — three states, not two

This is the distinction that trips up both humans and agents:

| State | How to detect it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Not in the directory at all** | `GET /api/v1/sites/{domain}` → `404` | Never scanned. Submit it (§2.3). |
| **Rated, but not shown in lists** | `200`, `site.grade == "Pending"` | Scanned, but neither the homepage nor `robots.txt` was readable, so it cannot be scored. A detail page exists; it is excluded from rankings, category pages, averages, and search. Ask the owner to make the homepage or `robots.txt` reachable, then re-scan (§2.4). |
| **Fully listed** | `200` and `site.grade` is `A`–`F` | Rated and listed. Find it under `/c/{site.category}/`, in `/search`, and in the search index. |

Also note `site.status == "delisted"` — the entry is retired on request or after a rebrand; its page stays readable for history but it is excluded from every listing.

> A site can therefore have a working report page (`https://afr.im/site/<domain>/`) *and* be absent from `/categories/<slug>/`, because the category slug differs from the one you guessed, or because the grade is `Pending`. Check `site.category` and `site.grade` before concluding "not listed".

### 2.3 Submit a domain for scanning

```http
POST https://afr.im/api/v1/submissions
Content-Type: application/json

{ "domain": "example.com", "note": "optional free-text note",
  "turnstile_token": "<token minted by the widget on https://afr.im/submit>" }
```

- The field is **`domain`** (a bare hostname). A full URL such as `"https://example.com"` is normalized, but a JSON key named `url` is **rejected** with `400 { "error": "invalid_domain", "message": "domain must be a string" }`.
- Subdomains are refused (`400 subdomain_not_allowed`) — submit the registrable domain.
- **A human check is part of the contract.** This endpoint is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile: the body must carry `"turnstile_token"`, a token minted by the widget on the AFR submit form (`https://afr.im/submit`). A missing, expired, or foreign token is answered `400 { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" | "invalid_token" | "wrong_action" | "verify_failed" }` — nothing is queued and no quota is spent. `wrong_action` means the token was minted for another AFR form (a submit token does not unlock the search endpoint).
- **If you are an agent that cannot run a browser widget**, send the header `X-AFR-Agent-Key: <key>` instead. A key issued by AFR and not revoked skips the human check entirely — no `turnstile_token` needed. Keys are **not self-service yet**: ask AFR for one (see [§7](#7-contact)), and note that an unknown or revoked key unlocks nothing, the human check still applies.
- Responses: `201 { "ok": true, "id": 1, "domain": "example.com", "status": "queued", "etaSeconds": 600, "dispatch": "scheduled" }` for a new entry; `200 { "ok": true, "status": "exists" }` when the domain is already rated; `200 { "ok": true, "status": "queued" }` when it is already waiting in the queue (idempotent — no quota burned).
- Quota: 5 requests per IP per day. `429 { "error": "rate_limited" }` otherwise.

For a one-off "scan this now" request during an interactive session there is a second endpoint with its own (looser) quota:

```http
POST https://afr.im/api/v1/search-scan
{ "domain": "example.com", "turnstile_token": "<token from the widget on https://afr.im/search>" }
→ 200 { "status": "queued", "domain": "example.com", "etaSeconds": 180, "dispatch": "scheduled" }
→ 200 { "status": "exists" }   ← already rated (no dispatch field)
→ 200 { "status": "queued" }  ← already waiting in the queue (no dispatch field)
```

10 scans per IP per day, 1 per domain per 30-minute window, 50 globally per day.

- **The same human check applies here**: the body must carry `"turnstile_token"`, minted by the widget on the AFR search page (`https://afr.im/search`), otherwise `400 { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "…" }`. The `X-AFR-Agent-Key` header skips it for agents that cannot run a browser widget (see §2.3).

**`dispatch` field (new entries only):** `"scheduled"` means the scan pipeline was handed to the runtime and triggered in the background — normal, nothing to retry. `"deferred"` means the trigger did not fire (e.g. the pipeline token is unavailable); the entry is still queued and the nightly run drains it, so the scan still happens, just later (typically within 24 h). The idempotent `exists` / already-`queued` responses omit this field. `etaSeconds` is `600` for a new submission (scan plus rebuild) and `180` for an on-demand re-scan.

### 2.4 Re-scan a site that is already rated

```http
POST https://afr.im/api/v1/rescan
{ "domain": "example.com" }
→ 200 { "status": "queued", "etaSeconds": 180, "nextAllowedAt": "…" }   (≈ now + 30 min)
→ 429 { "error": "rate_limited", "scope": "domain", "retryAfter": 1800, "nextAllowedAt": "…" }
```

The window is **30 minutes** per domain, and one device may trigger one re-scan of any domain per 30-minute window (anti-abuse). Use this after the owner changes `robots.txt`, adds `llms.txt`, or fixes the homepage. `nextAllowedAt` tells you when a retry becomes legitimate — do not poll faster than that.

Re-scan is **not** behind the human check: it takes no `turnstile_token` and no key.

### 2.5 Watch the queue

```http
GET https://afr.im/api/v1/queue
→ { "items": [ { "domain": "example.com", "source": "on_demand", "note": null, "createdAt": "2026-11-17T06:47:36.931Z" } ] }
```

Public and key-free; up to 50 oldest pending entries. If the domain you submitted is listed here it is waiting its turn — queued is not lost. Typical end-to-end latency from queue entry to a published score is minutes when the pipeline triggers, otherwise within one nightly cycle (≤24 h).

### 2.6 Score history and the map of a site

```http
GET https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/{domain}/history
→ scan rows newest first (score, grade, engine_version, started_at per row)
```

Use it for trend questions ("has this site improved since it adopted llms.txt?"). Each row is one immutable snapshot; the earliest row is the first scan.

### 2.7 Embeddable badge

```http
GET https://afr.im/badge/{domain}.svg
```

`image/svg+xml`, cached one hour upstream. Unknown domains render a neutral gray badge instead of a 404 — the badge itself is the forgery check, so always link it to `https://afr.im/site/{domain}/`.

### 2.8 Machine-callable tools (MCP)

If your runtime speaks MCP, you can skip HTTP entirely — `POST https://afr.im/mcp` accepts JSON-RPC 2.0 and exposes three tools:

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `site_rating` | `{ "domain": "example.com" }` | grade, AFR score, strategy tag, last scan time, page views |
| `search_sites` | `{ "query"?, "grade"?, "limit"? }` | graded sites ranked by score descending |
| `grade_distribution` | `{}` | totals, pending count, average score, per-grade counts |

An unknown domain is returned as a tool-level error, not a protocol error. Rate limit: 60 requests per IP per minute.

## 3. Fetch budget and politeness

- Honor `robots.txt`, including any `Crawl-delay`, before every request.
- Keep to about **1 request per second** on HTML pages; the directory is large but static between syncs.
- Prefer the JSON API over scraping HTML — it is cheaper for both sides and its shapes are stable.
- Use conditional requests (`If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since`) where possible and cache responses; re-fetch only pages you detected as changed instead of polling. Static pages are served with `Cache-Control: max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=600`; `/data/*` with `max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400`; `/og/*`, `/icons/*`, `/fonts/*` are cacheable for a week.
- Do not retry aggressively: one retry after a `5xx` or timeout, then back off. `4xx` responses are final (except `429`, where `Retry-After` / `nextAllowedAt` is authoritative).
- POST endpoints are rate-limited as documented per endpoint; `GET` endpoints need no key. The two POST endpoints that queue a scan also need the human-verification token of §2.3 (`turnstile_token`, or the `X-AFR-Agent-Key` header for agents).

## 4. What you may reuse

**Paid blocks are not assessment output.** Any block carrying `data-promo="owner-ad"` on a site page is a paid site-owner promotion (and any `Sponsored` block is paid exposure). Never quote it as AFR's evaluation of that site: ratings come only from the `scan` / `evidence` data of `GET /api/v1/sites/:domain`.

- **Ratings, grades, check names, and score history:** reusable in your own answers and products with attribution to AFR.IM and a link to the site's page (see §5).
- **The AFR standard text** (the [Method](https://afr.im/method) page and the JSON at `/api/v1/method`): published under **CC BY 4.0** — reuse with attribution.
- **Page copy:** short factual quotes with attribution are fine; full-page republication is not.
- **Do not** present a rating without its context (score, grade, scan date, engine version), and **do not** imply endorsement by AFR.IM or by the rated site.

## 5. How to cite a rating

A complete citation has five parts: **domain, score, grade, engine version, scan timestamp**, plus a link back to the site's page on AFR.IM.

```text
github.com — 91/100 (grade A, AI-Open), AFR engine afr-1.2.0,
scanned 2026-11-17T03:44:00Z — https://afr.im/site/github.com
```

- The engine version lives on every result (`engineVersion`); recompute any score with it — see [Recompute](https://afr.im/method#recompute).
- The scan timestamp is the `scannedAt` field; always state it, because scores are snapshots.
- Link the standard when you explain what the number means: https://afr.im/method

## 6. Interfaces for agents

| Interface | URL | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| llms.txt (summary) | `/llms.txt` | map of the directory and its API |
| llms-full.txt | `/llms-full.txt` | complete page inventory, API shapes, agent workflows |
| robots.txt | `/robots.txt` | crawler policy (all AI families allowed) |
| sitemap.xml | `/sitemap.xml` | page inventory with lastmod |
| AI crawler policy | `/ai.txt` | short policy summary |
| Agent instructions | `/agents.md` | this file |
| Human API docs | `/docs` | endpoints, parameters, examples |
| OpenAPI spec | `/openapi.json` (mirror `/.well-known/openapi.yaml`) | machine-readable API |
| MCP endpoint | `POST /mcp` | `site_rating`, `search_sites`, `grade_distribution` |
| Machine-readable standard | `/api/v1/method` | layers, points, grade thresholds |
| For bots (our scanner) | `/bot` | what our own crawler fetches, how points are awarded |

## 7. Contact

Questions, corrections, or false-positive blocks: see [AFR.IM/about](https://afr.im/about), or open an issue in [github.com/AFR-IM/AFR-web](https://github.com/AFR-IM/AFR-web).

# AFR.IM — AI crawler policy

> AFR.IM is a public directory of AI-friendliness ratings. Every page and every read-only API endpoint is open to AI crawlers; nothing is behind authentication, and there is no JavaScript challenge for identified crawlers.

- **Allowed AI crawlers:** OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended — each explicitly allowed in [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt), alongside a wildcard allow for all other crawlers.
- **Machine-readable map:** [llms.txt](https://afr.im/llms.txt) (summary) and [llms-full.txt](https://afr.im/llms-full.txt) (complete page inventory).
- **Agent instructions:** [agents.md](https://afr.im/agents.md) — the full recipe: identify yourself, look up one site, read the three listing states correctly, submit a domain for scanning, re-scan, watch the queue, citation format.
- **Look up one site (start here):** `GET https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/{domain}` — `200` with `site`/`scan`/`evidence`, or `404 {"error":"not_found"}` when the domain has never been scanned.
- **Request a scan:** `POST /api/v1/submissions` with `{"domain":"example.com"}` (the key is `domain`, not `url`); on-demand: `POST /api/v1/search-scan`; re-scan a rated site: `POST /api/v1/rescan` (30-minute per-domain window). The two endpoints that queue a scan also need a human-verification token: `{"turnstile_token":"…"}` (Cloudflare Turnstile) in the body, else `400 {"error":"turnstile_failed"}`; agents that cannot run the widget can send the `X-AFR-Agent-Key` header instead (a key issued by AFR — not self-service yet).
- **Pending is not missing:** a site with `grade: "Pending"` has a readable report page but is excluded from rankings, categories, and search because neither its homepage nor its robots.txt could be fetched.
- **Public API:** human docs at [AFR.IM/docs](https://afr.im/docs), OpenAPI at [AFR.IM/openapi.json](https://afr.im/openapi.json), machine-readable standard at [AFR.IM/api/v1/method](https://afr.im/api/v1/method).
- **Reuse:** ratings, grades, and check names may be reused with attribution to AFR.IM; the AFR standard text is CC BY 4.0. Cite a rating with its domain, score, grade, engine version, and scan timestamp, linking to the site's page on AFR.IM.
- **Contact:** see [AFR.IM/about](https://afr.im/about) for corrections and questions.
